requirements_addressed: Create keycloak role with LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE properties
Create keycloak database owned by keycloak role

Password from psql variable (:kc_password), never hard-coded

completion_promises.criterion_text: `deploy/keycloak/init-keycloak-db.sql` creates role `keycloak` (login, **non-superuser**, NOCREATEDB/NOCREATEROLE) and database `keycloak` owned by it
completion_promises.evidence: The SQL file deploy/keycloak/init-keycloak-db.sql already exists and creates the keycloak role with LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE properties (lines 69) and creates the keycloak database owned by the keycloak role (line 91). Comprehensive tests validate all role properties including non-superuser status, inability to create databases/roles, and login capability.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Creation is idempotent (guarded against `pg_roles`/`pg_database`) — a second apply is a clean no-op
completion_promises.evidence: The SQL file uses SELECT EXISTS queries against pg_roles (line 62) and pg_database (line 84) to check for existence before creation. Uses psql \if conditionals (lines 65-71, 87-93) to skip creation if objects already exist. Tests validate idempotency by applying the SQL twice and verifying no errors occur on second application (TestIdempotency class).

completion_promises.criterion_text: The role password is taken from a psql variable / env, never hard-coded or committed
completion_promises.evidence: Password is provided via psql variable :kc_password (line 69 of SQL) which is passed with -v flag during execution (documented in line 19-20). The test suite verifies no hard-coded passwords exist in the SQL file (TestPasswordFromVariable::test_sql_file_contains_no_hardcoded_passwords) and confirms the role has a password set (TestPasswordFromVariable::test_role_has_password_set).

completion_promises.criterion_text: The script includes/documents the least-privilege proof: the `keycloak` role is denied `SELECT` on `study_tutor` learner tables and can reach only its own `keycloak` database
completion_promises.evidence: Lines 96-201 of the SQL file document and implement least-privilege isolation. The script revokes all privileges from PUBLIC (lines 113-114), grants CONNECT only to owning roles (lines 117-118), and explicitly revokes cross-database access (lines 121-124). Lines 170-186 include verification queries proving keycloak cannot connect to study_tutor. Lines 189-201 document the negative proof (connection attempt that must fail). Comprehensive test suite validates all isolation aspects (TestLeastPrivilegeIsolation class with 5 tests).

completion_promises.criterion_text: The DB name and role name match the §4 KEYCLOAK_DB contract exactly (`keycloak` / `keycloak`)
completion_promises.evidence: Both role and database are named exactly 'keycloak' (lines 69 and 91 of SQL). The test suite validates exact naming with TestNamingContract class, which verifies both role name (test_role_name_is_keycloak) and database name (test_database_name_is_keycloak) match the contract exactly.
